Image: Crypto News Pepeto Announces a Security Upgrade While the XRP Price Set To Rise Despite the Anthropic IPO Pulling Money Out of Crypto

DUBAI, United Arab Emirates, Nov. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Pepeto released a security upgrade for its exchange this week, and within days the presale passed $11.29 million. The upgrade is only part of the story, because the more telling detail shows up in the presale flows, where addresses tied to large XRP holdings have taken positions far too big to be test buys. Investors with that kind of history do not commit at that size unless they expect a return.

The XRP price, and the money leaving crypto for the Anthropic IPO, explain what the wider market is doing this week. They also explain why the addresses with the longest track record chose to enter now instead of waiting.

Crypto News: Pepeto's Upgrade Lands as the XRP Price and the Anthropic IPO Explain the Selloff

Why is XRP going down? The XRP price trades near $0.95 on November 21, after touching $0.89 on November 15, its lowest level since November 2024, and the cause is outside the token itself. Spot XRP ETFs lost $19.13 million in the week to November 13, the largest weekly outflow since March. That money left to buy Anthropic IPO shares, which had nothing to do with Ripple.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse made that point directly, and VanEck's Matthew Sigel described it as a capital vacuum draining every coin at once. So the drop came from money rotating into one stock while nothing inside XRP broke, and that money comes back once the shares are priced.

Will XRP go back up? Its record says yes, because XRP fell from $3.84 in 2018 to $0.11 by 2020, then climbed back to $3.84 in 2025. Traders keep naming $1 as roughly this cycle's floor, and most of them hold $10 as the long-run XRP price prediction. From $0.95, that is about 950% upside. The figure sounds huge, but the math is simple: $10 on 63.5 billion tokens gives a market cap near $635 billion, a level the largest crypto assets have already reached. On top of that, the weekly RSI divergence forming now is the first chart sign that selling pressure is easing.

So the XRP price points up over time, and holders have no reason to sell a dip that an IPO caused. But $10 is still a 10x from a $60.6 billion valuation, and a move like that takes years. The wallets that built lasting wealth in earlier cycles did it by buying projects at their earliest prices, and Pepeto's presale price is that kind of early entry today.

Pepeto's Security Upgrade Is the Reason XRP Whales Are Moving In

This week Pepeto made the security layer of its exchange stronger, and the presale passed $11.29 million in the same month XRP had its worst run in two years. Pepeto is a meme coin on Ethereum, built by an original Pepe cofounder, and the difference is simple: Pepe came with a joke, while Pepeto comes with trading tools.

This upgrade protects the AI risk scorer, which deals with a problem most traders still have, because they buy without checking the contract and some tokens let a buyer in but never let them sell. The scanner checks a coin before your money moves and blocks a trap token before it leaves your wallet, so the money that would have been lost stays with you.

The math explains why big money is paying attention, and anyone can check it. Taking XRP from a $60.6 billion valuation to $10 needs about $575 billion of new money. Pepeto at the presale price is valued near $80 million, so a small part of that money moves it much further. If it reached just half of Pepe's $11.4 billion record, that would be about 71 times today's price, and a $1,000 entry would turn into roughly $71,300. That same $1,000 buys you about 5.27 billion PEPETO today, and staking starts the moment you buy and pays around $1,600 a year at today's rate while you wait for the listing.

Conclusion

XRP is proven, and at a $60.6 billion valuation a 10x needs years and hundreds of billions of new money. Pepeto is still in presale, small enough that a part of that money moves it much further, and the catalyst for that move is the approaching Binance listing.

Every cycle ends the same way, with the people who followed big wallet activity early posting the gains, while those who waited buy at the prices the early wallets are selling.

For whoever considers Pepeto as strong project worth holding ahead of the market recovery, stages are closing faster every week, and the entry price climbs each time one fills, so investors who see that skipping it in 2026 could be this cycle's biggest regret are moving now.

data.title: India's Congress warns of more protests against Meta after clashes with police
data.description:
* Youth Congress workers storm Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai, Gurugram

* Protesters want leaders' Instagram accounts restored; two have been, many remain curbed

* Meta restricted over 5.4 million items in India in first half of 2026

(Tweaks lede, adds details of Congress Delhi protest banner, opposition reactions in paragraph 8, 10)

NEW DELHI, Nov 21 (Reuters) - The youth wing of India's main opposition Congress party on Saturday warned of more protests against Meta's removal of some accounts and posts of its members, a day after clashing with police outside the US firm's India offices.

Meta declined to comment on Friday's unprecedented protests, which marked an escalation by the influential political group in the company's biggest market by users. Debate is growing in India about potential risks to free speech from the increasingly strict efforts of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government to remove social media content it objects to.

Modi's government says it orders content to be taken down only if it breaches local laws, can harm public safety or national security. Congress has long accused Meta and other social media platforms of curbing dissent online by removing party accounts, favouring Modi's government.

Meta has said it restricts content in India to comply with local laws.

In Hyderabad on Friday, protesters carrying placards chanted slogans as they stormed into the building that houses Meta's offices, smashing plants to the ground and clashing with police, according to footage released by the Indian Youth Congress' X account.

Another video showed Congress workers spray-painting anti-Meta slogans on walls outside the building that houses its Mumbai office, clashing with security guards who tried to stop them. In Gurugram near New Delhi, Congress workers chanted slogans and held banners reading "restore youth Congress accounts", official online posts showed.

The Indian Youth Congress posted warnings on X that it would "storm your offices across the country and stage protests" unless Instagram accounts of its leaders are restored.

On Saturday, the Congress wing posted a video of its workers putting up a banner in central Delhi taking a dig at Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, referring to him as "Mark BJPberg" to allege the company's favouritism towards Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party.

India's IT ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

MODI'S PARTY ACCUSES CONGRESS OF VANDALISM

Telangana opposition politician K.T. Rama Rao criticised Congress workers over what he called vandalism at Meta's Hyderabad office, saying it had undermined the city's reputation as a safe destination for businesses.

Pradeep Bhandari, a national spokesperson for Modi's ruling party, criticised Congress' actions on Saturday, saying they had "not only vandalised and destroyed Meta's office in Hyderabad" but were also "flaunting it on social media".

"This is Congress Model: Vandalise offices of Private companies," he wrote.

Two such accounts were restored after Friday's protests, but thousands of accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government remain restricted, Manu Jain, who is in charge of social media for the youth group, told Reuters on Saturday.

Meta must explain how its algorithms restrict posts and must restore accounts taken down on government orders, he added.

Reporters Without Borders has said the removal of journalistic content from social media has been on the rise in India this year, and free speech activists say a new government rule gives social media companies hardly any time to review and decide on takedown requests.

In February, Modi's government ordered social media companies to take down unlawful content within three hours of being notified about it, tightening an earlier 36-hour timeline.

Meta disclosures show that it restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India under local laws in the first half of 2026, second only to Indonesia and up from about 70,000 in the whole of 2025.

"The large majority of these items included instances where we were obligated to proactively restrict content... based on local law requirements," Meta said.

(Reporting by Aditya Kalra and Munsif Vengattil; Editing by William Mallard)

data.title: Persona Earns CEN/TS 18099 High Certification for Injection Attack Detection
data.description:
Independent evaluation of Persona's Android SDK confirms defenses against deepfakes and other injected media at the top level of the first standard

SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Persona, the leading global identity platform, today announced that its Android SDK has earned CEN/TS 18099 High certification for injection attack detection (IAD). High certification  is the top level of the European standard. The evaluation was run by CLR CERT, the certification body of Cabinet Louis Reynaud (CLR) Labs. CLR Labs is accredited under ISO/IEC 17025, the international standard for testing laboratories, and it edits CEN/TS 18099. This certificated injection attack detection is available to all Persona customers and can be activated by working with Persona's team.

Injection attacks skip the camera entirely. Instead of holding a photo or mask up to a lens, fraudsters use virtual cameras, emulators and tampered devices to feed stolen, manipulated, or AI-generated media straight into the verification flow. To the system, the result looks like a real live capture, and traditional liveness checks aren't built to catch it.

"Our customers are facing more sophisticated deepfakes, face swaps and replay attacks while their identity verification volumes grow rapidly," said Irfan Faizullabhoy, product manager at Persona. "Earning CEN/TS 18099 High is one way we're helping them stay ahead of both, with independently tested defenses that work at scale."

A demanding, independent evaluation

The European Committee for Standardization (CEN) published CEN/TS 18099 in 2024 as the first standard for testing injection attack detection. It grades systems at three levels: Basic, Substantial and High. To test at the High level, evaluators spent at least 30 person-days attacking Persona's Android SDK. They used at least three injection methods, including rooted devices, tampered camera services and custom operating system builds. They also used at least 15 types of attack media, including deepfake videos, AI-generated faces and spliced video clips. Evaluators checked that real users could still verify, so a system couldn't pass just by blocking everyone.

"CLR CERT congratulates Persona on achieving High-level compliance under the CLR CERT IAD certification program for CEN/TS 18099," said Kévin Carta, director of CLR Labs. "As editor of the European standard on biometric injection attacks, we built this evaluation to test defenses against injected video, tampered apps, and modified operating systems. In a constantly changing digital world, compliance is more essential than ever. We are honored that Persona selected CLR CERT."

Built for fraud teams, invisible to real users

Persona's injection attack defenses run automatically and in real time. Users take a short guided selfie while Persona analyzes video, device and camera signals in the background to confirm a live person is in front of a real camera. Fraud and risk teams get clear reason codes, such as "virtual camera detected," so they can explain each decision during audits and appeals.

"Deepfake submissions keep growing in volume and sophistication, but agentic AI is an even more alarming trend," said Daniel Lee, product lead at Persona. "We're seeing more real-time phishing attacks where bad actors mimic verification flows, trick people into submitting their government IDs and selfies and then try to inject that genuine media into legitimate sessions. That makes detecting and stopping injection attacks more critical than ever."

Meeting the EU's rising bar for remote identity proofing

The certification comes as the EU tightens its rules for remote identity proofing. The EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation, which covers remote customer identification, applies from July 10, 2027. European identity-proofing standards, including ETSI TS 119 461 for trust service providers, already point to CEN/TS 18099 testing.

Persona's certification is listed on the CLR CERT certified products list at clr-cert.eu/produits_certifies. To learn more, visit: https://withpersona.com/blog/persona-achieves-cen-ts-18099-high-certification 

Customers can turn on certified injection attack detection by contacting their Persona account team.

About Persona

Persona is an identity platform that helps organizations keep the internet safer and more accessible for real people and businesses. Organizations use Persona to securely collect, verify, manage and make decisions about the identities of individuals, businesses and agents, with AI-backed orchestration that automates and streamlines the process from end to end. Backed by Persona’s own research into emerging threats, its fraud prevention and identity theft protection have stopped more than 300 million fraud attempts, including synthetic identities, account takeovers and deepfakes.

Founded in 2018 and headquartered in San Francisco, Persona has verified roughly 1 billion identities and is available in more than 200 countries and territories and 20 languages. Persona supports consumer-facing businesses across a variety of sectors, including LinkedIn, OpenAI, Twilio, Square, Udemy, Travelex and Gusto. For more information, visit withpersona.com.

data.title: EU leaders' chair proposes new cuts to EU 2028-2034 budget draft, suggests digital tax
data.description:
* Costa proposes 3% digital tax on online advertising and intermediation turnover

* Proposal cuts seven-year EU budget by €40 billion to €1.582 trillion versus October draft

* EU leaders discuss plan on November 26 to 27 aiming for December agreement

By Jan Strupczewski

BRUSSELS, Nov 21 (Reuters) - The chairman of European Union leaders proposed further cuts to the European Commission's draft EU 2028-2034 budget on Saturday and suggested new revenue streams for the EU, including a digital tax, to help finance EU policies.

The cuts proposed by Antonio Costa, who chairs summits of EU leaders, would reduce the overall seven-year budget by €40 billion to €1.582 trillion compared to a proposal presented by the Irish EU presidency in October and by €180.6 billion compared to the original Commission proposal.

Costa's proposal mainly cuts the European Competitiveness Fund - aimed at helping make European industry more competitive against China and the United States - defence and external spending. Money for agriculture and cohesion is relatively protected compared to the Irish compromise proposal.

Nevertheless, France criticised the new numbers as not sufficiently protecting farmers, and the European Parliament's chief budget negotiator, Siegfried Muresan, said the numbers were a step backwards.

"This proposal is unacceptable to Parliament and cannot form the basis for our consent. The EU budget is an investment budget. Cuts, more cuts and a side of cuts are not an investment strategy," he said.

EU leaders will discuss Costa's proposals at a special summit on November 26-27 with a view to narrowing differences between the EU budget's net contributors and net beneficiaries, and to reaching an agreement in December.

The EU budget is how the 27-member bloc finances all its policies - from supporting farmers to developing new technology and supporting industry and research against competition from China and the US.

It also covers student exchanges, equalising standards of living across the EU, help for Ukraine and EU officials' salaries, among others.

DIGITAL TAX A PROPOSED NEW REVENUE

The EU budget is financed from national contributions and the so-called "own resources" - taxes and levies that are collected by EU countries but are dedicated to the EU budget, such as customs duties, a percentage of value-added taxes or a tax on non-recycled plastic waste.

The more such "own resources" the EU budget has, the less governments have to contribute from national coffers.

Costa's proposal for the digital tax builds on a 2018 proposal by the European Commission that was not taken up by EU governments at the time.

Costa has now proposed that the EU put a 3% tax on the annual net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services and user-generated data for companies with an annual turnover for digital activities of €50 million in the EU and a global turnover of over €750 million.

This would mean taxing mostly US-based digital giants such as Google, Microsoft ( MSFT ), Meta, Apple or Amazon ( AMZN ), a move many EU governments have been wary of for fear of angering US President Donald Trump, who has spoken against such a tax.

To find more money, Costa proposed slowing down the repayment of the capital of the more than €600 billion that the EU will have jointly borrowed by the end of 2026 for its post-pandemic recovery fund.

The repayment of the interest and capital will start in 2028 and last until 2058 as initially planned, but the repayment of capital may be slower in the first seven years to leave more money in the budget for other priorities, officials said.

The budget and its sources of revenue must be agreed unanimously and it is often an acrimonious battle. The seven-year ​2028-2034 budget under discussion now is particularly difficult because of additional pressures on national ⁠budgets from high energy prices and defence spending.

Although the EU budget only has to be ready for 2028, leaders want a deal by the end of 2026 because there are elections next year in France, Italy, Poland, Greece, Estonia, ⁠Finland ​and Slovakia, with the budget likely to play a role in electoral ​campaigns.

(Editing by Timothy Heritage)

data.title: Entain in talks to sell remainder of CEE business to CVC, Sky News reports
data.description:
Nov 21 (Reuters) - Ladbrokes owner Entain ( GMVHF ) is in advanced talks to sell its remaining stake in its central and eastern Europe operations to private equity firm CVC Capital Partners in a deal that could value the division at between £1.5 billion and £1.75 billion ($1.96 billion to $2.29 billion), Sky News reported on Saturday, citing sources.

Here are some details:

* Entain ( GMVHF ) holds a 47.5% stake in the CEE business, having offloaded a 20% interest to joint venture partner EMMA Capital in June for €425 million ($466.1 million)

* Entain ( GMVHF ) said at the time it would keep evaluating options to fully exit the business, which owns SuperSport in Croatia and STS in Poland

* According to Sky, there are other interested parties

* Entain ( GMVHF ) is under pressure to cut costs to offset increases in Britain's gambling taxes. It expects an extra £25 million hit to its UK and Ireland retail business after the government raised taxes on the industry for a second consecutive year in last month's budget

* Entain ( GMVHF ) declined to comment on the report, while CVC did not immediately respond to a request for comment sent outside regular business hours

data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Tech leads global stocks rout, Treasury yields fall
data.description:
(Updates to US stock market close)

* Broad index of global stocks in biggest weekly drop since 2020

* Anthropic shares fall as much as 14.5% to just above IPO pricing

* US bonds rally, spot gold and silver at 14-month lows

* US chipmakers, Taiwan stocks each fall 17% for the week

By Rodrigo Campos

NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Tumbling technology-related shares led a global stock sell off on Friday, with US traders searching for safe havens as the US 10-year yield dropped by the most in a month.

Traders sold stocks in most markets with Japan and Korea down more than 5% overnight. Taiwanese shares were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1990, while on Wall Street chip-maker shares fell 10.7% Friday and 17.1% for the week.

Anthropic, which debuted this week, fell as much as 14.5% on its first full day of trading, just above its $83 IPO pricing, and ended down 9.1% at $88.30.

Consumer staples was the sole S&P 500 sector to end in the black on Friday.

"Markets are entering a more defensive phase," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

"Strong AI demand and successful individual listings are no longer sufficient to sustain broader risk appetite when investors are questioning valuations, borrowing costs and the outlook for corporate profitability."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 949.73 points, or 1.93%, to 48,147.33; the S&P 500 fell 265.44 points, or 3.70%, to 6,910.39, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 1,261.47 points, or 5.28%, to 22,617.73.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 34.89 points, or 3.30%, to 1,021.91. Its weekly decline of 8.1% was the largest since early 2020.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 2%, emerging market stocks fell 3.10% and MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan closed lower by 3.27%. Japan's Nikkei fell 5.06%.

The VIX index, linked to the cost of insurance against a drop in the S&P 500, closed at its highest since April 2025.

As investors sought safe-haven assets, government bonds rallied.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 10.43 basis points to 4.948%, the largest daily drop since October 22. The 30-year bond yield fell 6.81 basis points to 5.3329%. data.title: How Grand Theft Auto VI's launch surpassed expectations
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 21 (Reuters) - You can paint your bedroom walls. You can scuba dive and explore shipwrecks. You can go birdwatching and catalogue up to 62 different species. You can even rob banks and steal cars, just like in the old days - but you'll need to be careful, because the police are smarter now and if you run out of gas, well, you'll have to fill up the tank.

The level of realistic detail in Rockstar Games' video game "Grand Theft Auto VI," which was released this week, has astonished gamers and helped the release roar beyond the already sky-high expectations that had built up after a 13-year wait and an estimated $1 billion production budget. It has a score of 99 out of 100 on Metacritic, the joint highest score of any game ever, and high praise for it has been almost universal.

"I feel like I truly have waited all this time and it's come, and for me, it's the ideal version of what they could have done," said Brandon Nightingale, a 34-year-old music production lecturer from Manchester in Britain and long-time fan of Rockstar Games.

"With the amount that they fit into the game I'm like, what do I do next? Do I do a mission or do I just go to the shop? Last night I played it and I just drove ... I'm just kind of soaking in the world."

Even rival developers were complimentary.

"Rockstar Games created a masterpiece that I am planning to explore in the coming weeks and months. Massive congratulations ... It is unbelievably hard to achieve what you just did," Michal Nowakowski, joint CEO of Poland's CD Projekt Red, developer of "Cyberpunk 2077" and "The Witcher" series, said in a social media post.

Pocketpair, the Japanese video game developer behind "Palworld," celebrated the release with an office sushi party on Thursday, and gave employees five days off to enjoy what it called a "new era of gaming."

The success of the game is a boost for Rockstar owner Take-Two Interactive Software ( TTWO ) and console makers Sony ( SONY ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ), but the significant media attention, something video games rarely attract, could also provide a turbocharge more generally for the sector.

Rockstar said on Friday that retail sales of the game reached a record $3.79 billion, their estimate as of the end of launch day. Many fans had preloaded the game ahead of launch, but sales will continue as the holiday season approaches. About three-quarters of sales so far have been on the PlayStation 5, with the rest on the Xbox Series X or S, said market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. A PC version is expected next year.

SCOTTISH ORIGINS

Back in the 1990s, GTA had its origins in a small office in Dundee, Scotland, said video games journalist Tom Regan. "It started off as a top-down, very arcadey game that was originally going to be a cops-and-robbers game, but then the developers realized it wasn't fun to play as police. It was more fun to cause mayhem.

"And to go from that, a very kind of tongue-in-cheek, crude game to the most incredible entertainment product in history that is really pushing interactive storytelling to new heights is incredible. It kind of just shows the growth of video games as a medium as well, artistically, commercially and culturally."

The action in GTA VI is set in Leonida, the game's take on Florida. Play switches between two leading characters, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval. They are partners in crime and romantically involved - just how romantically is up to the player.

The presence of Lucia, GTA's first fully fleshed-out female protagonist, reflects and may in turn have an effect on the changing demographics of gamers. Women will comprise an estimated 4 out of ​10 GTA VI players in the US, according to a ⁠Bain survey ahead of the release.

"In its early decades, GTA was a game overwhelmingly made by and played by young men," said Tore Olsson, a professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville. "Representations of women in those early games were sexualized, lacking nuance, and more wallpaper than anything else."

Just as the sophistication of the graphics and gameplay of the GTA franchise has progressed from its 1990s roots, so has its reflection of society as a whole, albeit retaining a satirical take on American culture.

"I played 'Vice City,' I played 'GTA San Andreas,' I played 'GTA IV' as well recently," said Mia Pazan at a GTA VI-themed sports event in Miami on Wednesday evening. "I'm Latina, and the reason I'm here right now is because we finally have actual mainstream Hispanic representations, and me personally, I really identify with Lucia a lot."

Some players on social media criticized the more inclusive direction, complaining that it was "woke" and expressing annoyance that one path open to Jason is being a supportive boyfriend who treats Lucia well. But ultimately most of the relationship options are choices that Rockstar gives the player, who can also decide to focus on committing crimes or any number of other possible paths.

Nightingale said some gamers would maybe miss the chaos of older GTA titles and their online multiplayer modes.

"Other people, like myself, I want the immersion of the world that they build," he said.

data.title: Bitcoin nodes could be stalled by repeating one ID 50,000 times. AI found the bug
data.description:
An AI tool built by Jack Dorsey’s Block found a way to temporarily stop a bitcoin node from processing messages from the network by feeding it one transaction ID, repeated 50,000 times.

Bitcoin Core, software used to run those nodes, disclosed the bug on Friday as CVE-2026-117348 and released versions 30.5 and 31.3 with fixes.

The advisory credits an automated AI scan conducted through Elias Rohrer’s Project Loupe at Spiral, Block’s open-source development unit, CoinDesk found.

Nodes are computers that check bitcoin payments and pass transactions and blocks to one another.

The pratical consequences of this issue were far reaching: An exchange relying on an affected node could be delayed in crediting deposits, while a miner could waste computing power working on an outdated view of the blockchain.

Core developers rated the bug as “medium severity” and “easily discoverable.” Under the security policy it adopted on Oct. 22, easily discoverable flaws receive fixes across maintained versions as soon as possible, with a public advisory alongside the releases, as CoinDesk reported.

How the trick worked

Bitcoin nodes hold on to orphan transactions, which are payments that spend coins from an earlier transaction the node has not seen yet. The node then goes looking for the missing pieces.

Since version 29.0, when another node announces one of these orphans, Bitcoin Core builds a list of its missing parent transactions and checks its records before deciding what to request.

Nodes announce transactions in batches of up to 50,000 entries. The software did not skip repeated entries.

An attacker could first send an orphan transaction with thousands of missing parents, then repeat its ID 50,000 times in one announcement. The receiving node would perform the expensive checks over and over.

“Each such message stalls the node for over a dozen seconds,” the advisory said. During that time, it processes no messages from other nodes, including new blocks. Sending further messages could prolong the disruption.

The fix makes the node process each transaction announced in a batch only once.

The policy reflects developers’ concern that AI tools make some vulnerabilities cheap for attackers to rediscover, reducing the protection offered by keeping fixes quiet.

data.title: Meta's India offices hit by opposition protests over account removals
data.description:
* Youth Congress workers storm Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai, Gurugram

* Protesters want leaders' Instagram accounts restored; two have been, many remain curbed

* Meta restricted over 5.4 million items in India in first half of 2026

NEW DELHI, Nov 21 (Reuters) - The youth wing of India's main opposition Congress party clashed with police outside Meta offices, protesting the company's removal of some Instagram accounts of its members, according to footage released by the group on Saturday.

Meta declined to comment on the protests, an escalation by the influential political group in the company's biggest market by users. Debate is growing in India about potential risks to free speech from the increasingly strict efforts of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government to remove social media content it objects to.

Modi's government says it orders content taken down only if it breaches local laws, can harm public safety or national security. Congress has long accused Meta and other social media platforms of curbing dissent online by removing party accounts, favouring Modi's government.

Meta has said it restricts content in India to comply with local laws.

MODI'S PARTY ACCUSES CONGRESS OF VANDALISM

Pradeep Bhandari, a national spokesperson for Modi's ruling party, criticised Congress' actions on Saturday, saying they had "not only vandalised and destroyed Meta's office in Hyderabad" but were also "flaunting it on social media".

"This is Congress Model: Vandalise offices of Private companies," he wrote.

India's IT ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

In Hyderabad on Friday, protesters carrying placards chanted slogans as they stormed into the building that houses Meta's offices, smashing plants to the ground and clashing with police, according to footage released by the Indian Youth Congress' X account.

Another video showed Congress workers spray-painting anti-Meta slogans on walls outside the building that houses its Mumbai office, clashing with security guards who tried to stop them. In Gurugram near New Delhi, Congress workers chanted slogans and held banners reading "restore youth Congress accounts", official online posts showed.

The Indian Youth Congress posted warnings on X that it would "storm your offices across the country and stage protests" unless Instagram accounts of its leaders are restored.

Two such accounts were restored after Friday's protests, but thousands of accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government remain restricted, Manu Jain, who is in charge of social media for the youth group, told Reuters on Saturday.

Meta must explain how its algorithms restrict posts and must restore accounts taken down on government orders, he added.

Reporters Without Borders has said the removal of journalistic content from social media has been on the rise in India this year, and free speech activists say a new government rule gives social media companies hardly any time to review and decide on takedown requests.

In February, Modi's government ordered social media companies to take down unlawful content within three hours of being notified about it, tightening an earlier 36-hour timeline.

Meta disclosures show that it restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India under local laws in the first half of 2026, second only to Indonesia and up from about 70,000 in the preceding six months.

"The large majority of these items included instances where we were obligated to proactively restrict content... based on local law requirements," Meta said.

(Reporting by Aditya Kalra and Munsif Vengattil; Editing by William Mallard)

data.title: Analysis-Wall Street banks set for banner year as Anthropic, SpaceX IPOs generate $1 billion in fees
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Wall Street banks are on track for one of their most lucrative years in the IPO business, with blockbuster listings by Anthropic and SpaceX generating more than $1 billion in underwriting fees alone.

A syndicate of 22 banks is set to collect about $550 million for underwriting Anthropic's $81.3 billion IPO, eclipsing the roughly $500 million they earned on SpaceX's record-setting offering in June, according to Anthropic's final offering prospectus published on Thursday.

The fees represent a relatively small share of the $81 billion Anthropic raised at its debut, or as much as $93.5 billion with overallotment options exercised. The banks will receive about 0.68% of the money raised in Anthropic's IPO, broadly in line with the roughly 0.67% they collected on SpaceX's offering.

Underwriting fees on IPOs typically run as high as 7% of proceeds, though the percentage drops sharply for bigger deals, with companies raising tens of billions of dollars able to negotiate significantly lower rates than smaller issuers.

ANTHROPIC'S FEE POOL

Anthropic's fee arrangements also highlight the bargaining power that blockbuster issuers hold over Wall Street.

Some banks working on the deal did not learn how much they would earn until Wednesday night, according to a person close to the transaction - suggesting an unusual degree of uncertainty until the final stages of the offering, even as banks compete fiercely over the most coveted deals.

Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment.

While it is common for IPO fees to be finalized when an offering closes, it is unusual for a company not to communicate in advance an approximate percentage of the offering that underwriters can expect to receive, the person said.

Other high-profile issuers have kept banks in the dark until the final stages of an offering, using intense competition among underwriters for roles on prized deals.

SoftBank-owned chip designer Arm did not provide banks with a clear fee arrangement when it hired 28 underwriters for its $5 billion IPO in 2023, Reuters reported at the time. SoftBank waited until days before pricing to spell out the fee structure, giving it a better sense of how the banks had performed during the marketing process, according to a person familiar with the information.

Banks are willing to accept relatively low fees on mega-IPOs because of the prestige of working on landmark listings, the boost to their league-table rankings and the potential for additional business, including stock trading, lending and wealth management services.

Anthropic is paying $536.7 million of the underwriting fees, with the remaining $13.3 million paid by its seven co-founders, who sold shares in the offering, the prospectus showed.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, which jointly led both the Anthropic and SpaceX IPOs, are set to take home the largest share of the fee pool, receiving roughly 20.5% each, or 41% combined, amounting to more than $110 million each. The remaining fees will be split among the other banks involved in preparing the AI company's public debut.

MEGA-IPOS

Banks have already had a lucrative year from public offerings. Global IPOs raised more than $357 billion this year, according to Dealogic, up from $186 billion in 2025, with SpaceX and Anthropic alone accounting for about half of that.

That marks the second-biggest year for IPOs according to Dealogic data going back to 1995, behind 2021's haul of $609 billion.

Revenue from US IPOs for banks is also at its highest in five years, Dealogic data shows. Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan lead the rankings and have each earned more than $330 million so far this year excluding Anthropic's IPO, up from about $260 million apiece in 2025.

That is still far below 2021, when the three banks earned more than $1 billion in fees each and total US IPO revenue for US banks hit almost $10 billion, according to Dealogic.

The 2021 total was pushed up by a pandemic-era boom fuelled by near-zero interest rates, stimulus-driven retail trading and a wave of listings of blank-check companies.

(Reporting by Sabrina Valle and Echo Wang, editing by Deepa Babington)

data.title: US was warned of telecom security risks years before Salt Typhoon
data.description:
(Removes reference to T-Mobile data being stolen in paragraph 3)

Nov 19 (Reuters) - The US government was warned in a report it commissioned about major national security risks from weaknesses in the country's telecom networks in 2022, two years before sweeping Chinese-linked cyberespionage known as Salt Typhoon.

The report commissioned by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency said US telecommunications networks contained "major structural vulnerabilities" and could be compromised from anywhere in the world.

US officials have previously alleged that hackers targeted nine telecom companies, including Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile and Lumen, during the 2024 Salt Typhoon campaign. T-Mobile has acknowledged the company was targeted in late 2024 but has said it prevented attackers from accessing sensitive customer data.

The report, disclosed as part of a lawsuit, has been reviewed by Reuters.

Details of the report were first reported by Bloomberg News on Thursday.

The June 2022 report described US telecom infrastructure as one in a "perilous and untenable situation," and added that international interconnects could provide attackers with "trusted" access. "The fact that US national networks can be readily compromised from anywhere in the world is not yet widely understood."

CISA withheld the report from public release for four years and resisted congressional pressure to publish it, according to Bloomberg News.

The agency did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Ron Wyden, a Democratic senator from Oregon, pushed for the release of the report last year. He had said in a statement, "Congress would have had ample time to require mandatory cybersecurity standards for phone companies, in time to prevent the Salt Typhoon hacks" had the report been made public when it was first written.

(Reporting by Harshita Mary Varghese in Bengaluru; Editing by Joyjeet Das)

data.title: Honda, Toyota recall 1.6 million vehicles over Takata airbag rupture risk
data.description:
* Carmakers say no injuries or crashes related to current recall

* Recalls follow simulation showing degradation of airbag inflators

* Earlier recalls over Takata airbags linked to at least 28 deaths in the US

(Recasts with separate Toyota ( TM ) recall, NHTSA statement)

By David Shepardson

WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Honda ( HMC ) and Toyota Motor ( TM ) said on Friday they are recalling about 1.6 million cars, trucks and SUVs over a risk that Takata airbag inflators could rupture.

Honda ( HMC ) and Toyota ( TM ) both said there were no injuries or crashes tied to the vehicles being recalled, and there have been no airbag inflator ruptures. The automakers will replace the airbag inflators in the recalled vehicles.

There have, however, been at least 28 deaths in the United States and more than 400 injuries stemming from defective Takata airbag inflators since 2009, an issue prompting the largest auto recall in US history. All of those deaths involved airbag inflators without a drying agent. At least 20 of those deaths were in Honda ( HMC ) vehicles.

The vehicles in the current recalls have airbag inflators that contain a moisture-absorbing material - unlike the millions of vehicles recalled previously.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said analysis and inflator degradation simulation models conducted by independent testing groups allowed the automakers to act ahead of potential risks.

"Honda ( HMC ) and Toyota ( TM ) saw early evidence of degradation risk in certain of their vehicles and are currently conducting proactive recalls of vehicles," NHTSA said late Friday, adding that other automakers continue to conduct inflator analysis and testing.

The recall includes 810,592 older Honda ( HMC ) cars and SUVs in the United States and 790,000 Toyota ( TM ) vehicles worldwide, including 314,000 in the United States.

The Toyota ( TM ) recall includes 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 IS250, 2017 GX460, 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 Tundra, 2005-2007 Sequoia and 2016-2017 4Runner. The Honda ( HMC ) recall covers some 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Honda Civic, 2012-2013 Honda CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX and 2013 Acura RDX vehicles.

The Honda ( HMC ) recall covers vehicles originally sold or registered in 14 states or territories known for high temperature, humidity and large temperature fluctuations.

Over the past decade, two dozen major automakers have recalled more than 100 million vehicles fitted with Takata airbag inflators worldwide, including about 67 million vehicles in the United States.

Various automakers have also reported hundreds of injuries in vehicles since 2009 from Takata airbag inflators that can explode, unleashing metal shrapnel inside cars and trucks, killing or injuring drivers or other vehicle occupants.

Honda ( HMC ) said long-term monitoring and analysis revealed potential propellant degradation in certain inflators within specific geographic regions.

Toyota ( TM ) warned that degraded propellant could cause the inflator to rupture if the airbag deploys and cause serious injuries.

The Honda ( HMC ) recall applies to vehicles sold or registered in Alabama, California, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Louisiana, Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas, Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands, Northern Mariana Islands (Saipan), Guam and American Samoa.

Toyota ( TM ) did not specify in which US states the recall applies but said it expects the replacement inflators will be ready by early 2027.

data.title: Mexican cell carriers facing widespread outages, users report
data.description:
MEXICO CITY, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Mexican cellphone users reported widespread service outages on Friday affecting Telcel, AT&T Mexico and Movistar, marking the latest disruption to mobile networks in the country.

Users began reporting problems around 11 a.m. local time, including an inability to make calls, loss of cellular signal and problems accessing mobile data, according to outage-tracking platform Downdetector.

-- Spokespeople for America Movil and Movistar did not immediately respond to requests for comment

-- AT&T Mexico said its network was "operating normally" and that any difficulties communicating with customers from other carriers were "due to reasons unrelated to our network"

-- The disruption comes just over a month after users reported outages in mid-October including loss of cellular signal and problems with calls and mobile data

data.title: Waymo recalls self-driving cars over closed freeway lanes, manual traffic control
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Alphabet's self-driving unit Waymo said on Friday it is issuing two recalls for its robotaxis over incidents involving closed freeway lanes and manual traffic control.

Earlier this week, Waymo said it halted operations of its vehicles on US freeways, after a California regulator barred its vehicles from freeways in the state.

The California ban, which took effect last week, is a result of a series of incidents where Waymo robotaxis entered active construction zones, the California Department of Motor Vehicles said.

Waymo said a statement it filed two safety recalls with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Thursday on its automated driving system "to strengthen how the Waymo Driver navigates closed freeway lanes and intersections with manual traffic control."

The closed freeway lanes recall stems from unusual circumstances where a Waymo vehicle may enter and continue driving in a closed freeway lane, the company said, adding it is still working on the recall remedy. Waymo said there were no collisions or injuries reported from the closed freeway events.

The manual traffic recall is to ensure self-driving vehicles better responds to manual commands at intersections from law enforcement or other emergency personnel and follows a collision in which a Waymo followed directions from an officer, but the officer was then temporarily obstructed. That update was completed on November 6.

Waymo says its technology outperforms statistically comparable human benchmarks and drastically reduces injury-causing crashes.

Last week, NHTSA said it opened a recall query into Waymo vehicles after numerous ‌incidents of its robotaxis passing stopped school buses.

The probe will look into nearly 3,000 company-owned self-driving vehicles. Investigators want to determine whether a software update Waymo rolled out late last year failed to stop ​its driverless cars from passing school buses with flashing red lights. Most of ​the violations happened after the company said the remedy had been ⁠deployed.

Separately, NHTSA and the National Transportation Safety Board have opened probes after one of Waymo's self-driving vehicles struck a child in January near an elementary school ⁠in ​Santa Monica, California.

(Reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Chris Reese and Diane Craft)

data.title: Nvidia's accounting is a focus of US SEC investigation, sources say
data.description:
(Refiles to fix company RIC in text in first paragraph)

By Chris Prentice and Alexandra Alper

NEW YORK/WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The US Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's ( NVDA ) accounting practices, said two people briefed on the matter, adding to the legal woes facing the scandal-hit chip giant.  

The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday reported that the SEC was probing Nvidia ( NVDA ) but said it could not ascertain the focus of the investigation. The people, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential issues, said SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing potential accounting issues at the company.

A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment. Spokespeople for Nvidia ( NVDA ) did not immediately respond to requests for comment. 

Prices of Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares extended losses and were down about 13% on Friday, according to LSEG data, after Reuters reported details of the SEC probe. They had been down more than 6% before Reuters published its report.

Reuters could not immediately determine when the SEC opened its inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog is examining. Investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without resulting in enforcement action. 

Still, the accounting focus of the probe, which Reuters is reporting for the first time, increases pressure on Nvidia ( NVDA ), whose investors are still reeling from revelations about ousted CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital relationships, including with Alice Huang, who US authorities suspect is a Chinese spy. China has denied she is a spy.

Alice Huang led Singapore-based Megaspeed, historically a large Nvidia ( NVDA ) chip customer, people familiar with the matter have said. US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over possible violations of export controls related to alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, the US Justice and Commerce departments said this week. 

The crisis has sent shares in Nvidia ( NVDA ), a linchpin of the AI boom, tumbling more than a third and stoked calls in Washington for tougher action on tech threats posed by Beijing. 

Megaspeed has said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and that it conducted "lawful business." Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.

The SEC probe is the latest of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) legal woes. The Justice Department has also been reviewing Nvidia's ( NVDA ) $12.9-billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face alongside a broader antitrust investigation into the company's acquisitions and practices, Reuters reported last month.

SINGAPORE ACCOUNTING CHANGE BACK IN FOCUS

Last year, Nvidia ( NVDA ) changed how it reports geographic revenue, using customer headquarters rather than billing addresses, which it said would better reflect the geographic profile of its revenue. The change resulted in Singapore being removed from its geographical breakdown. 

The Financial Times, citing company accounts, reported on Tuesday that Nvidia ( NVDA ) had made the change even as Singapore sales soared to almost half its global revenue. 

That accounting shift has drawn renewed press scrutiny in the wake of the Alice Huang scandal.

Southeast Asia has become a hub for chip smuggling to China since the Biden administration barred advanced AI chip exports to that country over concerns they could boost Beijing's military.

Analysts and investors have also grown increasingly concerned about circular AI financing deals, in which chipmakers including Nvidia ( NVDA ) have pursued complex financial arrangements to help customers fund purchases of their chips and the construction of costly AI infrastructure, such as data centers. Nvidia ( NVDA ) has backed AI companies and cloud providers and provided guarantees connected to data-center projects that use its equipment. 

Critics say such arrangements can make it harder for investors to assess the quality of chipmakers' revenue and their true financial exposure. Speaking to Reuters last month, SEC enforcement chief David Woodcock said the agency was examining AI companies' corporate disclosures to ensure issuers are giving investors the full picture on potential risks.

On its Tuesday earnings call, Nvidia's ( NVDA ) interim CEO and former CFO Colette Kress said the company was proud of its role in supporting the AI industry, but would be far more selective moving forward about AI industry financing deals. 

The SEC under President Donald Trump has pulled back on enforcement, saying it will focus on bread-and-butter securities fraud, including accounting violations that have long been a mainstay of its enforcement work. It recently launched a new financial reporting and accounting unit within its enforcement division, aimed at developing cases in accounting and auditing areas.

(Reporting by Chris Prentice in New York and Alexandra Alper in Washington; Additional reporting by Karen Freifeld and Jody Godoy in New York; Editing by Michelle Price and Daniel Wallis)

data.title: Wonder explores sale of Grubhub, Wall Street Journal reports
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Wonder, a food delivery startup led by former Walmart executive Marc Lore, is exploring a sale of Grubhub, The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Bankers have contacted Walmart, Target ( TGT ), Kroger ( KR ) and other retailers about a potential acquisition, the report added.

Wonder acquired Grubhub in 2024 for $650 million, including $500 million of senior notes and $150 million in cash. The price was a fraction of the $7.3 billion that European meal delivery group Just Eat Takeaway paid for the business in 2020 during the pandemic-driven boom in food delivery.

A potential sale would come amid broader consolidation in the food and grocery delivery industry.

Rival DoorDash agreed in October to acquire Instacart in a $17 billion deal to strengthen its position in the fast-growing U.S. grocery delivery market as competition among app-based delivery platforms intensifies.

Earlier this year, Grubhub sold its college-campus food delivery business to DoorDash for $300 million. DoorDash also invested $125 million in Wonder as part of the transaction.

There are no guarantees a deal will come together, The Wall Street Journal said, citing the people.

Wonder, Walmart, Target ( TGT ) and Kroger ( KR ) did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

data.title: Wall St ends sharply lower on AIÂ selloff, S&P 500, Dow in correction
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US stocks extended their rout on Friday, and the S&P 500 and the Dow both confirmed corrections after Anthropic's momentous debut fell flat, exacerbating worries about the AI trade that has driven this year's stock market rally.

All three major US equity indexes ended sharply lower. The Dow and the S&P 500 are now more than 10% below their record closing highs, confirming both indexes have entered a correction.

The bellwether S&P 500 notched its seventh consecutive drop, its longest losing streak since February 2020.

The S&P 500 and the Dow logged their largest weekly percentage losses since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced his market-rattling "liberation day" tariff package.

The Nasdaq's weekly drop was its largest since March 2020. The tech-heavy index has dipped into negative territory for the year.

"This is clearly a challenging day for capital markets, and as we head into a Friday close, appears to be accelerating to a certain degree," said Bill Northey, senior investment director at US Bank Wealth Management in Billings, Montana. "But as we step back and evaluate fundamentals and sentiment, sentiment is clearly winning the day today."

"Sentiment is always the more powerful force in the immediate space, whereas fundamentals tend to win out over time," Northey added, referring to economic strength and solid corporate earnings, among other things.

Anthropic's supersized debut as a publicly held company, which was intended to raise as much as $2 trillion in market cap, failed to catch fire on Thursday, closing 17.1% above its $83 offer price as enthusiasm for the stock faded throughout the session.

In its second day as a publicly held company, Anthropic's shares fell 9.1%. Nvidia's shares tumbled 13.8%.

The Anthropic IPO, combined with Nvidia's quarterly earnings report, failed to dispel fears over risks associated with artificial intelligence and the massive expenditures on the nascent technology.

"Nvidia reported what might have been one of the greatest quarters in corporate earnings history; they did everything right," said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services in Hammond, Indiana. "A lot of people, myself included, were looking to the Anthropic debut to some extent as a clearing event, and it wasn't."

The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index , which has powered much of the broader stock market's gains in recent months, was up as much as 106.6% in mid-June. That luster has faded, with the index's year-to-date advance having shrunk to 18.7%.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon fell 3.9%, while Meta dropped 5.9%.

Neocloud firm CoreWeave fell 12.1% and its peer Nebius slid 16.1%.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 949.73 points, or 1.93%, to 48,147.33, the S&P 500 lost 265.41 points, or 3.70%, to 6,910.42 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 1,261.47 points, or 5.28%, to 22,617.73.

The CBOE Market Volatility Index , often referred to as Wall Street's "fear gauge," rose to its highest close since April 7, 2025.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said the central bank's policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels.

Markets are pricing a near-certain likelihood of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike at the Fed's next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Among other movers, Intuit shares fell 12.8% after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.

UnitedHealth rose 2.8% after TD Cowen upgraded its shares to a "buy" from a "hold" rating.

The AI selloff also sent Caterpillar 5% lower on worries over weakening demand for its power-generating and backup power equipment.

Cryptocurrency firms including Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood tumbled between 6.3% and 9.6% after bitcoin dropped below the $60,000 level.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.77-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 38 new highs and 1,199 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 928 stocks rose and 3,964 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 4.27-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 3 new 52-week highs and 28 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 21 new highs and 826 new lows.

Volume on US exchanges was 25.19 billion shares, compared with the 19.50 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: RxERP Outlines What the FDA’s Move to 12-Digit NDCs Means for Pharma Product Data
data.description:
New overview and checklist help teams review product matching, barcode data, and trading-partner workflows ahead of the 2033 change

ST. GEORGE, Utah--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- RxERP, the serialized enterprise resource planning platform purpose-built for the pharmaceutical supply chain, today released a 12-Digit NDC readiness overview and companion checklist to help pharmaceutical companies prepare their product records and workflows for the FDA’s new 12-digit NDC format. The resources build on RxERP’s support for 10-, 11-, and 12-digit representations of a product’s NDC within one product record, helping manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors, and 3PLs keep product identity consistent as formats change.

The operational challenge begins when trading partners identify the same product differently. A supplier’s code may fail to match the version stored in the receiving system, requiring a manual lookup or prompting creation of a duplicate item. Those duplicates can split inventory counts, lot history, and pricing across records. Adding a new NDC format makes reliable product matching essential across receiving, inventory, orders, and traceability data.

Under the FDA’s final rule, the uniform 12-digit NDC takes effect March 7, 2033, with a labeling transition through March 6, 2036. The rule itself leaves HIPAA standards unchanged, while the FDA expects billing standards to accommodate 12 digits by 2033.

The transition also changes how systems connect National Drug Codes with Global Trade Item Numbers, or GTINs, used in serialized workflows. The existing NDC-based GTIN structure cannot embed a 12-digit NDC. Software that extracts an NDC from a GTIN will therefore need to change how it associates the identifiers with the correct product and packaging level. GS1 application identifier 715 provides a way to carry the NDC as a separate barcode data element alongside the GTIN.

“A product shouldn’t become two products because a trading partner sent its NDC in a different format,” said Steve Madsen, founder and CEO of RxERP. “We connect those NDC formats to one product record so teams can maintain a consistent product identity. These resources help companies identify the remaining work across barcodes, integrations, and trading partners while they have time to plan and test.”

The overview explains the conversion rules, the GTIN mapping challenge, and actions for manufacturers, repackagers, distributors, 3PLs, and pharmacies. The companion checklist turns that guidance into a working assessment, with space to record test results, document evidence, assign owners, and set follow-up dates. Teams can use it to test whether their systems can:

  • Match original and converted NDCs to the correct product and package record while preserving strength, dosage form, and package differences.
  • Preserve leading zeros and handle newly assigned 12-digit NDCs without misclassifying them as UPCs.
  • Interpret GS1 AI (715) through both the scanner and receiving application while continuing to process existing barcodes.
  • Exchange identifiers correctly with trading partners and follow a product through receiving, inventory, an outbound order, and serialized-data workflows.

RxERP brings product records, serialized data, inventory, and orders into the same platform, with serialization built into operational workflows. Its FDA NDC API integration brings FDA product data into the item master, and product setup draws on FDA and GS1 data to reduce manual entry. Keeping NDC representations associated with one product record provides a foundation for the broader barcode and trading-partner work required by the transition.

Read the 12-Digit NDC overview and download the working checklist at https://rxerp.com/12-digit-ndc-transition/

RxERP helps pharmaceutical manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors, 3PL providers, and pharmacies expanding into distribution streamline operations, to reduce manual processes, support compliance workflows, and scale with greater visibility and control. data.title: GTCR explores potential takeover of payments firm Global Payments
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - GTCR is exploring a potential takeover of payments processor Global Payments ( GPN ), the private equity group said in a filing on Friday, days after reports that a consortium effort with CD&R was dropped.

Shares of Global Payments ( GPN ) closed the day 10% higher. It was up about 19% so far in 2026.

GTCR is working with other private equity firms to finance the potential deal, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters. GTCR, which holds a 16.35% stake in Global Payments ( GPN ) and is the largest shareholder, said no definitive decision has been made.

Global Payments ( GPN ) did not immediately respond to Reuters request for a comment.

Private equity firms CD&R and GTCR had dropped their pursuit of Global Payments ( GPN ) as a buyout consortium, Reuters reported earlier this month, citing people familiar with the matter.

The report had added that it was possible that CD&R and GTCR will resume the talks with Global Payments ( GPN ) at a later date or another buyer for the company may emerge.

Atlanta-based Global Payments ( GPN ) is one of the world's largest payment processors. It enables merchants to accept card and digital payments and provides software and technology services to businesses. Its market value stood at about $22 billion, as of last close.

The company has faced pressure in recent years from slowing growth in some business lines, intensifying competition and investor demands to boost profitability.

Bloomberg News reported the potential takeover deal first and said it could value Global Payments ( GPN ) at $50 billion, including debt and premium.

(Reporting by Pritam Biswas in Bengaluru; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli)

data.title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Drives Comcast, Charter to Record Traffic
data.description:
06:22 PM EST, 11/20/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Comcast ( CMCSA ) and Charter (CHTR) reported some of their busiest internet days as players preloaded Grand Theft Auto VI ahead of its Thursday launch, Bloomberg reported Friday.

Comcast ( CMCSA ) said traffic on Wednesday was 31% above an average day and 9.6% higher than its previous peak. At one point, nearly a quarter of its internet traffic was tied to downloading and playing the game, Bloomberg reported.

Charter said traffic rose 49% since preloads began Nov. 10, with the game accounting for more than 12.6% of peak network traffic. Take-Two said it sold 32.5 million copies in presales, according to Bloomberg.
